links.outcome: Response appropriateness for lay-language versus medical-terminology phrasing of equivalent breast symptom questions
links.effect: ChatGPT-3.5 responses were appropriate for 7/7 (100%) common acute breast symptom questions when phrased both colloquially and using standard medical terminology.
links.quote: ChatGPT-3.5 generated responses were appropriate for 7/7 (100 %) questions regarding common acute breast symptoms when phrased both colloquially and using standard medical terminology.

links.outcome: Adherence of LLM breast symptom advice to ACR guidelines and clinical judgment, rated by breast radiologists
links.effect: Appropriate for 7/7 (100%) common symptom questions, but only 3/9 (33%) pregnancy-associated breast symptom questions and 3/4 (75%) palpable abnormality management/imaging questions.
links.quote: In contrast, ChatGPT-3.5 generated responses were appropriate for 3/9 (33 %) questions about pregnancy-associated breast symptoms and 3/4 (75 %) questions about management and imaging recommendations for a palpable breast abnormality.

links.outcome: Consistency of responses across three repeated submissions of each question
links.effect: Responses were scored 'unreliable' if inconsistent across three submissions; overall results were appropriate for 100% of common, 33% of pregnancy-related, and 75% of palpable abnormality questions.
links.quote: Questions were submitted three times to ChatGPT-3.5 and all responses were assessed by five fellowship-trained breast radiologists.

screen.reason: Evaluates ChatGPT-3.5's appropriateness on acute breast symptom questions phrased in lay vs medical language, scored by breast radiologists, but does not test a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice intervention.
